claims: The Artemis II mission features a 10-day "figure-8" trajectory.
The Artemis II mission takes four astronauts from Earth orbit to the Moon and back.
Artemis II launches from Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
Orion completes two elliptical orbits around Earth to check systems before committing to the Moon.
The SLS rocket launches Orion on a trajectory toward the Moon.
The Orion spacecraft uses a trans-lunar injection burn to head toward the Moon.
Orion loops around the far side of the Moon roughly 4,600 miles beyond it.
Orion uses lunar gravity to "boomerang" back to Earth.
The Artemis II mission is designed as a free-return.
Gravity naturally pulls the spacecraft back toward Earth without needing major maneuvers in the Artemis II mission.
The spacecraft travels ~244,000 miles back to Earth.
The spacecraft enters the atmosphere at ~25,000 mph.
The spacecraft utilizes a "skip-entry" technique to manage heat.
Artemis II reentry speed is ~25,000 mph (~40,000 km/h).
Artemis II splashdown location is Pacific Ocean near San Diego.
Artemis II maximum distance from Earth is approximately 252,799 miles.
Artemis II maximum distance from Earth is further than Apollo 13.
